text: Palmistry is a traditional practice kept here for reflection and entertainment. It is not a science: researchers regard it as a pseudoscience, and books disagree with one another about what the lines mean.
A palm reading cannot say anything about health, illness or medical conditions, and it should never replace a doctor.
The life line is not a measure of how long anyone will live. That is a common myth; here it is read only as a theme of energy and vitality.
A palm reading is not financial guidance. It cannot say anything about money, investments or what will happen with money.
A palm reading is not career advice and should not be used to make decisions about work. It speaks only in general traditional themes such as temperament.
A palm reading is not relationship advice and cannot say what will happen with another person. The heart line is read only as a theme of emotional style.
No line says what will happen to anyone. Palmistry here describes themes to reflect on and never predicts events, dates or outcomes.

Many hands have no distinct fate line or sun line. A line that was not seen is not described at all, and nothing is read into its absence. A line marked uncertain was only faintly or partly seen, so only a loose idea of its theme is given.
Lines in a photo can be missed or misread, which is why each one is marked detected, uncertain or not visible. A clearer photo, in even daylight with the palm flat and in focus, usually helps.
